newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Orbital begins suit over R&D policy.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Orbital begins suit over R&D policy.

text.p: Orbital Engine Corp Ltd said on Friday it had instructed its lawyers to launch a A$12.5 million lawsuit over changes to the federal government's research and development incentive scheme.

Orbital managing director Tony Fitzgerald told Reuters Orbital had given the government's Industry Research and Development (IR&D) Board until Thursday to provide a satisfactory response to Orbital's outstanding IR&D syndication application.
"We have received no reply and we have instructed our solicitors to go ahead with the legal action," he said.
"The application was put in in November last year and it usually takes three months to approve but there was a lot of going backwards and forwards," Fitzgerald said.
"In May we were told there would be a special meeting of the IR&D Board to resolve the A list of 46 outstanding applications," he said.
"We were on top of that list but when the meeting was held no applications were approved," he said.
"We were told there would be another meeting but the government announced it was changing the legislation the day before it was to be held."
Legislative amendments to give effect to the federal government's new policy on R&D incentives was tabled in Parliament yesterday.
Fitzgerald said he had been informed the legislation was "highly retrospective" and did not recognise syndicate applications like Orbital's which already had financing schemes in place.
"Our application related to a project to apply Orbital's combustion process to existing four stroke engines to achieve lower emissions and improved fuel consumption," Fitzgerald said.
"We believe it should be processed under the existing legislation but failing that we will be seeking compensation," Fitzgerald said.
